through: 2026 Week 8 for current-season references; all featured moments are completed 2016–2025 results
designIntent: Exactly one source-backed, readable signature achievement per manager; gold only for championship winners. No awards or standings are inferred from incomplete 2026.

Stilly.headline: From 0–4 to a Fellas championship
Stilly.story: Four losses to open the season, then an 8–6 finish and a fourth-seed title run. The Kupp-for-Evans-and-Henry trade supplied 44.98 combined semifinal points from those two acquired starters.

Stew.headline: The 11-win favorite who finished one step short
Stew.story: Stew won 11 regular-season games and earned the top seed before finishing second to Stover. The recorded championship result was affected by the NFL's canceled Buffalo–Cincinnati Week 17 game.

Thommy.headline: The original dynasty returned for ring No. 4
Thommy.story: After winning three straight titles in 2016–2018, Thommy survived a 2.30-point 2024 semifinal and won the championship over Stilly, 205.30–114.88.

Stover.headline: Gurt finally climbed the mountain
Stover.story: Stover went 9–5, entered as the No. 2 seed and earned the league's official 2022 title over Stew. The archived final score comes from the NFL's interrupted Week 17 schedule.

Birch.headline: The runner-up became the champion
Birch.story: After losing the 2018 final by 4.96 points, Birch went 11–2 in 2019 and edged Stew by 4.72 points to claim his first championship.

Tony.headline: The trades, the stars, and a 4.30-point final
Tony.story: Tony followed a 4–10 season with a 10–3 campaign and a championship win over Evans, 138.28–133.98. Joe Mixon's 29.50 points led the title-game starters.

Mitch.headline: Thirteen wins. One loss. No trophy.
Mitch.story: Mitch won 13 of 14 regular-season games in 2025, scoring 1,894.88 points, but finished third rather than winning the title. He reached championship finals in 2020 and 2023.

Kuhl.headline: A third-place season worth remembering
Kuhl.story: Kuhl went 8–6 and finished third in 2022—one of his clearest verified achievements. The record reflects real postseason placement, not a hypothetical title.

JMid.headline: A league-leading offense from day one
JMid.story: JMid joined in 2024—not 2023—and went 8–6 while leading the league in regular-season points scored. The previous franchise slot belongs to Evans.

Scott.headline: A second-year manager takes the crown
Scott.story: After a 5–9 debut in 2024, Scott went 8–6 in 2025 and beat Thommy 156.32–86.00 in the final. Bijan Robinson scored 38.40 and Brock Purdy added 36.92 in the title-game lineup.
